Definition: from G1097; knowing (the act), i.e. (by implication) knowledge:--knowledge, science.
BiblicalUsage: gnōsis is a plain word for knowledge, science. In Luke 1:77, the text says "To give knowledge of salvation unto his people by the remission of their sins." In Romans 2:20, the text says "which hast the form of knowledge and of the truth in the law."
TheologicalSignificance: I take gnōsis to mean that wisdom begins with fearing the Lord, and it shows in how we live, not just what we know. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
